headline: Shifting Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift electricity costs, including capacity auction and distribution infrastructure investments, from residential ratepayers to large energy users like data centers, potentially saving residential customers money.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Dominion Energy (with amendments).
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia governor signs Dominion-backed bills. All eyes on regulators now.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and allows Dominion Energy to spend on burying distribution lines. The bill aims to shift capacity market costs and distribution infrastructure investments to high-load users, potentially saving residential customers money.

headline: Mandatory Water Use Reporting for Data Centers
short_summary: This bill requires water users providing water to data centers with air permits to report monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities concerned about water resources, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden, historically sought to keep water use secret).
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including those addressing water usage, to regulate data centers in Virginia. SB 553 specifically mandates that water providers disclose the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, supplied to data centers to the State Water Control Board.

headline: Regulating Data Center Location and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including noise studies for nearby residential areas and schools, and allows for assessment of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates, Delegate Josh Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (concerned about increased study mandates and potential delays).
news_headline: What does Data center site assessment and sound profile for high energy use facilities (HB153) do?
news_summary: HB 153 requires Virginia local governments to review potential impacts before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more of electricity. Applicants must submit a site assessment studying noise and effects on nearby homes and schools, and localities may also request reviews on water, farmland, parks, historic sites, and forests.
